tagline: Natural gas and oil producer with integrated gathering, processing and transportation infrastructure
hero_kpi_rationale: Spectacular 174% increase in natural gas sales to $7,433 million in 2025, primarily driven by the Southwestern merger and higher natural gas prices
company_description: Expand Energy Corporation operates as an independent natural gas production company in the United States. The company engages in acquisition, exploration, and development of properties to produce oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids. It holds interests in the Marcellus Shale in the northern Appalachian Basin in Pennsylvania; the Marcellus and Utica Shales in Ohio and West Virginia; and the Haynesville and Bossier Shales in Louisiana and Texas. Expand Energy Corporation was formerly known as Chesapeake Energy Corporation and changed its name to Expand Energy Corporation in October 2024. The company was founded in 1989 and is based in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

risks.title: Management Changes
risks.summary: Management changes may lead to shifts in company strategy and direction, which could impact financial performance.
risks.score_rationale: Leadership transition with appointment of Michael A. Wichterich as Interim President and CEO on February 6, 2026, replacing Domenic J. Dell Osso, Jr. may impact strategy and operations. (Position in the 10-K: Item 1A)

risks.title: Commodity Price Volatility
risks.summary: The company is highly exposed to commodity price fluctuations, which could materially impact financial results.
risks.score_rationale: Company heavily dependent on natural gas and oil prices, with $2,031 million of incremental revenue in 2025 driven by higher gas prices. Significant exposure to price fluctuations. (Position in the 10-K: Item 1A)

risks.title: Debt Obligations
risks.summary: The company has significant debt obligations inherited from the Southwestern merger, which could impact financial results if refinancing becomes difficult.
risks.score_rationale: Company assumed Southwestern's Senior Notes in merger, increasing interest expense to $235 million in 2025. Significant debt obligations may impact financial flexibility. (Position in the 10-K: Item 1A)

risks.title: Liquidity and Capital Management
risks.summary: The company has adequate liquidity ($4.1 billion) but must actively manage its funding needs following the Southwestern merger.
risks.score_rationale: As of December 31, 2025, company maintains $4.1 billion in liquidity including $616 million cash and $3.5 billion unused borrowing capacity. Adequate but requires ongoing management. (Position in the 10-K: Item 1A)

risks.title: Environmental and Regulatory Compliance
risks.summary: The company is subject to strict environmental regulations, which could impact financial results in case of non-compliance or contamination.
risks.score_rationale: Natural gas and oil operations subject to strict environmental regulations. Company has environmental risk assessment processes and provisions for contingencies. No material environmental proceedings disclosed as of December 31, 2025. (Position in the 10-K: Item 1A)

risks.title: Integration and Operational Risk
risks.summary: Successful integration of the Southwestern merger is critical to realizing expected synergies and maintaining market competitiveness.
risks.score_rationale: Southwestern merger substantially increased operations with doubled production and added oil/NGL capabilities. Integration success critical for realizing merger synergies. (Position in the 10-K: Item 1A)
